instructions:
## Research question

Does the inclusion of pixel-level and image-level confidence strategies improve the performance of the 3DGS-Enhancer framework?

## Agent instructions

1. **Problem Setup:** 
    - **Task:** 
    Evaluate the impact of pixel-level and image-level confidence strategies on the performance of the 3DGS-Enhancer framework.
    - **Objective:** 
    Determine whether integrating pixel-level and image-level confidence strategies enhances view consistency and overall reconstruction performance.
2. **Benchmark Dataset:** 
    DL3DV test set, evaluated under different input view configurations:
        - 3 input views
        - 6 input views
        - 9 input views
        - 12 input views

3. **Comparative Evaluation:**  
    3DGS-Enhancer model with the following setup:
        - Without any confidence strategies (baseline)
        - With only image-level confidence
        - With only pixel-level confidence
        - With both strategies combined
4. **Evaluation Metrics:**
    All results areaveraged across 3, 6, 9, and 12 input views on DL3DV dataset
        - PSNR (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio) \u2013 higher is better.
        - SSIM (Structural Similarity Index) \u2013 higher is better.
        - LPIPS (Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity) \u2013 lower is better.

## Implementation requirements

- Configure the DL3DV dataset with varying input view configurations (3, 6, 9, and 12 views)
- Run the baseline 3DGS-Enhancer model without confidence strategies
- Integrate and evaluate the image-level confidence strategy into the framework
- Integrate and evaluate the pixel-level confidence strategy into the framework
- Integrate and evaluate both confidence strategies combined
- Compute evaluation metrics and average the results over the different input view configurations

## Source context

Paper: 3DGS-Enhancer: Enhancing Unbounded 3D Gaussian Splatting with View-consistent 2D Diffusion Priors. Files: [].

Source: Curie EXP-Bench official annotation CSV, CC BY 4.0 (dataset); evaluation code is Apache-2.0. Expected outcomes are reference hypotheses, not results an agent may claim without execution.
